speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are experiencing severe abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, and dysuria; to help me pinpoint the cause, please tell me your age and gender first. Additionally, have you noticed any blood in your urine or changes in your urinary frequency?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old female. The patient presents with a 5-day history of severe abdominal pain and cramping, accompanied by nausea and vomiting. She reports pain with urination and also experienced burning pain during sexual intercourse 3 days ago. She mentions being sexually active with one male partner, using condoms inconsistently.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Pelvic Inflammatory Disease (PID). The combination of severe abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, dysuria, and specifically the history of dyspareunia (pain during sex) in a sexually active young female is highly suggestive of PID. REQUEST IMAGES: Pelvic_Ultrasound. REQUEST TEST: Urinalysis, Chlamydia/Gonorrhea NAAT, and CBC with differential.
